title: Father's jitney buses in Atlantic City
summary: His brothers go to Shaw University, and his father buys horse-drawn buses to carry people between the cabarets of Atlantic City's back bay.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, my brothers were much older now, they had started going away to school. Because they had a little difficulty going to the high schools in -- especially in the Catholic high school, at that time in Philadelphia. They weren't at the place where "JACK THE BEAR" WILSON.

they was acceptin' blacks in the high schools. See, they thought, when they finish the elementary school, that was enough for them. That would enable them to read so they wouldn't give their boss no poison, and that was enough. They didn't need to go to high school.

So, there was a school in Raleigh, North Carolina, called SHAW Shore University. But, it was academic, too. So my father got the money together some way, and they went to school. But this year when they come back from school, he had a bright idea. He bought a couple of busses. In Atlantic City they called at the time, what we'd call NICKEL ET TES or now, jitneys, but it was a bus, you know. And their horse and team. So this was, I imagine, about 1905, or 1908, and like in through there. Well, there wasn't any NO automobiles then of any consequence. Only the very rich had automobiles. So most of our people, especially on the back bay in Atlantic City, they had these busses, and they did all their transportation. You carried your -- you'd crawl on a bus and say, "I want to go to Indiana Avenue." And at Indiana Avenue, you'd say, "I want to go up to Virginia Avenue, or Maryland Avenue.", and the fellow got 25¢ or something for taking you up there.
Well, my father, he decided to do that with the people. And here's what happened. So, at night, I used to go ride with my brother when they worked late at night, see. And they'd go

to a place just like -- there was a place called Scott's, and there was a place called the Bay State. And there was a place called Boathouse, and then like these places were running then. And so, the busses would stand up there at these places, and when somebody'd party'd come out, if they were too drunk to walk or something like that, they'd take a bus ride goin' home.
